newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rally late after finance firm denials.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rally late after finance firm denials.

text.p: Thai stocks, which fell sharply for most of Friday, staged a late rally at the close as some finance firms hit by rumours denied they were in trouble and speculative buyers swooped in on cheap buys, brokers said.
Mostly finance counters were bought, they added.
"The market mood improved slightly after some finance firms came out and denied market rumours that they faced liquidity problems," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The SET index, which hit a day low of 710.23-point, finished 1.55 points higher at 727.56 on 5.2 million baht turnover.
The SET-50 index gained 0.22 point to 53.65. Decliners led gainers 154 to 139, while 125 issues were unchanged.

Top Thai finance firm Finance One Plc and Ekkapat Finance and Securities Plc denied the rumours after the lunch break. There have been market worries about the quality of finance firm loans to the depressed Thai property sector.

"Although denials were made by some finance firms earlier today on the rumours, investors were worried about non-performing loans that may be suffered by finance firms which property developers might be unable to settle," Payuha said.

Brokers said some investors also stayed away from long-term investment ahead of a visit here next week by officials of Moody's Investors Service to study Thai data before arriving at a decision whether to downgrade Thailand's long-term debt ratings.
Large capitalised Finance One topped the active list, falling 1.75 baht to 23.75, after going limit down earlier, and Krung Thai Bank dropped one to 38.50.
Support for the index was seen by some brokers at around 700 on Monday while resistance was put at 740.
